lawyer:

full_judgment:
Mr. Muhammad Imman Ali, .J: This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the Order dated 16.08.2010 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No.397 Of 2007 allowing the application for converting the First Appeal filed under Order XLI Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure into First Miscellaneous Appeal under Order XLIII Rule 1(e) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 2. Short facts contended in the application. are that inadvertently and out of bona fide mistake the learned Advocate for the appellant-applicant has preferred the First Appeal No.397 of 2007 under Order XLI Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure challenging the judgment and decree dated 30.5.2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No.82 of 2001 instead of First Miscellaneous Appeal. It is contended that at the time of hearing of the appeal the learned Advocate for the appellants for the first time upon hearing the learned Advocate for the respondents, realized that he had mistakenly preferred First Appeal instead of First Miscellaneous Appeal against the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge 1st Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No.82 of 2001. It is further contended that the First Appeal No.397 of 2007 was filed because of bona fide mistake of the learned Advocate for the appellant-applicants and that, there is no latches or negligence on the part of the appellant applicants in the matter, and unless the First Appeal is treated as a First Miscellaneous Appeal. the appellant-applicants will suffer irreparable loss and injury. 

 5. Mr. S. N. Goswami, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in not considering the facts and circumstances that since the judgment and order dated 03.10.2007 in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.298 of 2007 have been passed by this Division to the effect that "the appeal shall be disposed of afresh on merit." The High Court Division had, in fact, no option in law but to hear the appeal on merit and the High Court Division cannot proceed to hear the application for treating the First Appeal filed under Order XLI Rule1 of the Code of Civil Procedure as First Miscellaneous Appeal under Order XLIII Rule 1(e) of the Code of Civil Procedure and as such the impugned judgment and order dated 16.08.2010 is liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate also submitted that in exercise of its discretion the Hon'ble High Court Division was not justified in allowing the application moved by the defendant appellant for treating the First Appeal filed under Order XLI Rule 1 of the 'Code of Civil Procedure as First Miscellaneous Appeal under Order XLIII Rule 1(e) of the Code of Civil Procedure because the Order XLI Rule 1 and Order XLII1 Rule 1(e) of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot mutually he exchanged by twisting even if the result to be achieved or relief claimed were analogous, and the settled law is that discretion must not be arbitrarily but should be judicial discretion  based on established legal principles and as such the impugned order dated 16.08.2010 is liable to be set aside. 

 9. It appears to us that the question of whether it should be a First Appeal or First Miscellaneous Appeal was not mooted before this Division when dealing with Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.298 of 2007. This Division directed the office of the High Court Division to register the appeal as per Rule. 

 10. However, it is our view that a direction to hear the appeal on merit does not preclude either party from filing any application which they consider necessary during pendency of that appeal. In the instant case the respondents filed an application for treating. the First Appeal as a First Miscellaneous Appeal. We find no illegality in filing such an application. By the judgment which is now impugned before us the High Court Division upon hearing both the parties allowed an application for treating the First Appeal filed under Order XLI Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure as First Miscellaneous Appeal under Order XLIII Rule 1(e) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 11. We do not find any illegality or infirmity in the decision given by the High Court Division. Whether or not a First Miscellaneous Appeal is maintainable in the facts of the case will be considered' in due course by the Bench dealing with the First Miscellaneous Appeal. The impugned order does not call for any interference by this Division. Accordingly the civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed, without, however, any order as to costs.
